summary: Created scripts/tests/ directory and ported all ~70 ledger plugin tests from persona-builder (tests/plugins/ledger.test.ts) into scripts/tests/ledger-plugin.test.js.

Used ESM import syntax (import { createRequire } from 'module') to bridge ESM test file with CJS source modules — required because Vitest 4.x is ESM-only and cannot be require()'d, while the ported source files use CommonJS module.exports.
All 50 tests pass with zero failures under `npx vitest run scripts/tests/`.
No imports reference persona-builder; all imports point to local personas/plugins/ledger/ modules via relative paths.
Test coverage spans all five required areas: roster rendering, MCP tools table rendering, role validation, note_only guard, and frontmatter templates / plugin hook composition.

comments.note: scripts/tests/ directory did not exist prior to this WP — it was created as part of this work. The vitest.config.ts already declares `include: ['scripts/tests/**/*.test.{js,ts}']` so new test files are picked up automatically with no config changes needed.

personas/plugins/ledger/*.js source files use CommonJS (module.exports / require) while Vitest 4.x is ESM-native. The `createRequire` bridge works correctly but means any future test files that want to import these CJS modules must use the same pattern. Consider adding a note in the scripts/tests/ README (or a brief comment in the test file header) to guide future contributors.

The root package.json has no `type: module` field, making all .js files CJS by default. However, Vitest transforms test files through its own pipeline, so ESM import syntax in .test.js works fine at test time. This is an implicit convention that may be non-obvious — a brief comment or docs note would help.

comments.note: renderRoster() will throw TypeError if called with null instead of an empty array. The onBuildContext guard (Array.isArray check) prevents this in production, but there is no test for null input. Low risk — callers always pass arrays — but a defensive guard or a documented contract would be cleaner.

validateRole() treats null role as an unknown string ('null') rather than silently skipping as it does for undefined. This is technically correct (null !== undefined) but could be surprising. Not a current issue since the YAML parser never produces null for a role field.

The scripts/tests/ directory is currently empty except for ledger-plugin.test.js. Future contributors adding tests must use the same createRequire(import.meta.url) bridge pattern when importing CJS source files. A brief comment or README in scripts/tests/ (already suggested by Developer) would prevent confusion.
